Package edu.uky.cs.nil.sg

Class ToolArguments

java.lang.Object
edu.uky.cs.nil.sg.ToolArguments
public class ToolArguments extends Object
An object for parsing an array of string configuration arguments to a story graph tool, such as the command line arguments passed to a Java main method.
Author:
Stephen G. Ware

    • contains

      public boolean contains(Option option)
      Checks whether a given option's key exists in this list of arguments. An option's key only exists in this list if it is preceded by a dash. For example, if the option's key is "o" then this method returns true only if "-o" is one of the arguments in this list. If the argument is found, it is marked used.
      Parameters:
      option - the option whose key is in question
      Returns:
      true if the option's key appears in this list, false otherwise

    • require

      public void require(String argument)
      Throws an exception if the given argument is not in this list. If the argument is found, it is marked used.
      Parameters:
      argument - the argument which must appear in this list

    • require

      public void require(Option option)
      Throws an exception if the given option's key is not in this list. An option's key only exists in this list if it is preceded by a dash. For example, if the option's key is "o" then this method returns true only if "-o" is one of the arguments in this list. If the argument is found, it is marked used.
      Parameters:
      option - the option whose key must appear in this list

    • indexOf

      public int indexOf(Option option)
      Returns the index of the given option's key in the original array of strings, or -1 if the option's key does not exist. An option's key only exists in this list if it is preceded by a dash. For example, if the option's key is "o" then this method returns the index of "-o" in this list. If the argument does exist, it is marked as used.
      Parameters:
      option - the option whose key index is desired
      Returns:
      the index, or -1 if the argument is not in the list

      public String require(int index)

    • getValue

      public String getValue(String key)
      Returns the argument immediately after the given key argument, or null if the key does not exist or has nothing after it. If the key is found, the key and the argument after it are marked used.
      Parameters:
      key - the argument whose value is desired
      Returns:
      the argument immediately after the given key

    • getValue

      public String getValue(Option option)
      Returns the argument immediately after the given option's key, or returns the option's default value if the option's key does not exist, or returns null if there is no default value. An option's key only exists in this list if it is preceded by a dash. For example, if the option's key is "o" then this method returns the argument after the argument "-o" in this list. If the option's key is found, the key and the argument after it are marked used.
      Parameters:
      option - the option whose key's value is desired
      Returns:
      the argument immediately after the option's key or the option's default value

    • requireValue

      public String requireValue(String key)
      Returns the argument immediately after the given key argument, or throws an exception if the key does not exist or has nothing after it. If the key is found, the key and the argument after it are marked used.
      Parameters:
      key - the argument whose value is desired
      Returns:
      the argument immediately after the given key
      Throws:
      RuntimeException - if the key does not exist or if it has nothing after it

    • requireValue

      public String requireValue(Option option)
      Returns the argument immediately after the given option's key, or returns the option's default value if the option's key does not exist, or throws an exception if there is no default value. An option's key only exists in this list if it is preceded by a dash. For example, if the option's key is "o" then this method returns the argument after the argument "-o" in this list. If the option's key is found, the key and the argument after it are marked used.
      Parameters:
      option - the option whose key's value is desired
      Returns:
      the argument immediately after the option's key of the option's default value
      Throws:
      RuntimeException - if the key does not exist and the option has no default value

    • checkUnused

      public void checkUnused()

      Throws:
      RuntimeException - if any argument in this list have not been used
